senses.definition: A bird that uses a strong bill to peck or chip wood.
senses.example: A woodpecker tapped on the trunk of a tall pine.

senses.definition: A wind instrument that starts its sound with air blowing across an edge or with one or two vibrating reeds.
senses.example: The flute is a woodwind even when made of metal.

senses.definition: The thick hair of a sheep or some other animals, or yarn and cloth made from it.
senses.example: The hat was knitted from soft wool.

senses.definition: A unit of a language you can speak, sign, or write, such as go or tree.
senses.example: I know the first word of the story.

senses.definition: To say or write something using particular words.
senses.example: I worded the question so younger players could understand it.

senses.definition: Using words or word sounds in a surprising way to make an effect or a joke.
senses.example: The riddle depended on wordplay about two things called a jam.

senses.definition: To spend effort doing a job or trying to reach a goal.
senses.example: Our group worked together to finish the model.

senses.definition: To do what something is supposed to do.
senses.example: The old flashlight will work with a fresh battery.

senses.definition: Effort or tasks done to make, earn, learn, or fix something.
senses.example: It took a lot of work to sort those cards.

senses.definition: Something created by an artist, writer, composer, or other maker.
senses.example: We read one short work by the poet in class.

senses.definition: To find the answer or decide what to do by thinking through a problem.
senses.example: We need to work out how to share 20 tokens among four players.

senses.definition: To go well or reach a good result.
senses.example: We hope the plan to move the concert indoors will work out.

senses.definition: To do exercise to build strength or fitness.
senses.example: My brother likes to work out before breakfast.

senses.definition: A book filled with activities or questions for practicing a subject.
senses.example: I finished two pages in my math workbook.

senses.definition: A room or building used for making and fixing things.
senses.example: Grandpa kept his tools in a small workshop behind the house.

senses.definition: A short class or meeting where people learn a skill by taking part.
senses.example: We learned to make paper boats at the library workshop.

senses.definition: Earth and the people, places, and living things on it.
senses.example: People all over the world play games with a ball.

senses.definition: A planet or other place that could be thought of as a whole, real or imagined.
senses.example: The story takes place on a world with two moons.

senses.definition: A large collection of linked pages and other resources that people can open over the internet.
senses.example: The browser helped me find a page on the World Wide Web.

senses.definition: An animal, such as an earthworm, that has a long, soft body and no legs.
senses.example: A worm wriggled into the loose soil.

senses.definition: To keep thinking about something that might go wrong, or to make someone feel that way.
senses.example: I worried that I would forget my lines.

senses.definition: A concern about what might happen or a feeling of being concerned.
senses.example: My biggest worry was finding my way back.

senses.definition: The value or usefulness of a thing.
senses.example: The guide helped us understand the worth of the old coins.

senses.definition: Good or useful enough to justify time, effort, or money.
senses.example: The hike was worth the effort when we reached the lookout.

senses.definition: Important or useful enough to deserve the time or effort involved.
senses.example: It was worthwhile to check one more shelf for the missing book.

senses.definition: To cover something by folding or winding material around it.
senses.example: We wrapped the glass jar in paper before putting it in the box.

senses.definition: A food made by folding a flat bread around a filling.
senses.example: I ordered a vegetable wrap for lunch.

senses.definition: A piece of paper, foil, or other thin material put around something to cover or protect it.
senses.example: I picked up the empty wrapper from the bench.

senses.definition: A ring made of leaves, flowers, or other decorations.
senses.example: A green wreath hung on the front door.

senses.definition: A badly damaged vehicle, ship, or other object, or what is left of it.
senses.example: We saw the wreck of an old boat at low tide.

senses.definition: To damage something so badly it no longer works or cannot serve its purpose.
senses.example: A cracked axle could wreck the cart.

senses.definition: To struggle with someone using holds, as in a sport, or to struggle to manage something.
senses.example: We watched the athletes wrestle on padded mats.

senses.definition: To work hard to understand or solve a difficult problem.
senses.example: I wrestled with the hardest clue for an hour.

senses.definition: To move by twisting the whole body or part of it quickly.
senses.example: The worm wriggled between two leaves.

senses.definition: To twist and squeeze something to remove liquid.
senses.example: Wring out the sponge before you set it on the shelf.

senses.definition: A small fold or line in cloth, skin, paper, or another surface.
senses.example: A wrinkle in the map hid part of the trail.

senses.definition: To form small folds or make a surface form them.
senses.example: I wrinkled my nose at the strong smell.

senses.definition: The joint that joins the hand to the arm.
senses.example: I wore a blue band around my wrist.

senses.definition: A strip or band worn around the wrist.
senses.example: We got a blue wristband when we entered the fair.

senses.definition: To make letters, words, or symbols so someone can read them later.
senses.example: I wrote her name on the envelope.

senses.definition: To create a story, song, message, or other work by deciding what words or notes go into it.
senses.example: We wrote a play about a lost robot.

senses.definition: To put words or numbers on paper or in a file so you can use them later.
senses.example: Write down your idea before you forget it.

senses.definition: Not correct or proper for the situation.
senses.example: I took a wrong turn and had to go back.

senses.definition: Unfair or harmful in a way people have a reason to object to.
senses.example: It is wrong to blame someone for a mistake you made.

senses.definition: Something done that is unfair or harmful.
senses.example: She tried to make up for the wrong by telling the truth.
